correctness.rationale: Starting from the exact one-dimensional source formula, mass normalization gives \(A(p)^p=p^p(2/(p-1))^{p-1}B(1/2,p-1/2)\). Differentiating \(F=\log A\) yields \(F'(p)=H(p)/p^2\), and another derivative gives \(H'=-1/(p-1)+p[\psi_1(p-1/2)-\psi_1(p)]\). The trigamma integral converts the bracket into \(4\int_0^\infty s e^{-(2p-1)s}/(1+e^{-s})\,ds\). The strict inequality \(1+e^{-s}>2e^{-s/2}\) gives the stated rational upper bound, which is strictly below \(1/(p(p-1))\); hence \(H'<0\) for every \(p>1\). The signs \(H(1^+)=+\infty\) and \(H(3/2)=4\log2-3<0\) give exactly one zero and therefore strict increase followed by strict decrease. I independently evaluated \(H'\) across the domain and recomputed the unique root \(1.317094285913839\ldots\); this numerical replay only corroborates the analytic proof.
